a01.title: Sukhmani, in Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru.
a01.salok: Salok. Ik Oankar: God is One, realised through the True Guru's grace. Salutation to the Primal Guru, who was before all. Salutation to the Guru who has been since the ages began. Salutation to the True Guru. Salutation to the revered, divine Guru.
a01.p1: Ashtapadi. Let me remember God in Simran (meditative remembrance of God), and, remembering him again and again, find peace, and so rid my body of strife and anguish. Let me remember the One, the Sustainer of the universe, whose Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is repeated by multitudes beyond counting. The Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis, pure words all, were made from the one word of the Lord's Name. The one in whose heart God places even a particle of it, his glory cannot be counted. Some long for one thing only, the sight of you; says Nanak, save me along with them.
a01.rahao: Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is God's Naam, the nectar of peace; it rests in the minds of the devotees.
a01.p2: Through Simran of God, one does not come to lodge in the womb again. Through Simran of God, sorrow and the messenger of Death flee. Through Simran of God, death keeps away. Through Simran of God, the enemy turns back. While remembering God, no obstacle at all can touch one. Through Simran of God, one stays awake night and day. Through Simran of God, fear takes no hold. Through Simran of God, pain does not torment. Simran of God is found in the company of the Saadh, the holy one. All treasures, says Nanak, are found in the Lord's love.
a01.p3: Through Simran of God come riches, spiritual powers and the nine treasures. Through Simran of God come knowledge, meditation and insight into the essence. Through Simran of God come chanting, austerity and worship. Through Simran of God, duality is destroyed. Through Simran of God, one has bathed at the places of pilgrimage. Through Simran of God, one is honoured in God's court. Through Simran of God, whatever happens is good. Through Simran of God, life bears its fruit in full. They alone practise Simran whom God himself moves to it. Says Nanak, I fall at their feet.
a01.p4: Simran of God is the highest of all. Through Simran of God, multitudes have been saved. Through Simran of God, craving is quenched. Through Simran of God, everything becomes clear. Through Simran of God, there is no terror of the messenger of Death. Through Simran of God, hopes are fulfilled. Through Simran of God, the mind's filth is washed away, and the ambrosial Naam settles in the heart. God dwells on the tongue of the holy. Nanak is the slave of the slaves of God's servants.
a01.p5: All who remember God are rich. All who remember God are honoured. All who remember God are accepted by him. All who remember God are the foremost of people. All who remember God depend on no one. All who remember God are kings over all. All who remember God dwell in peace. All who remember God become forever imperishable. They alone take to Simran to whom God himself is merciful. Nanak begs for the dust of the feet of such servants.
a01.p6: All who remember God do good to others. To all who remember God I am a sacrifice, always. All who remember God have radiant faces. All who remember God pass their lives in peace. All who remember God have conquered the self. All who remember God live a spotless life. All who remember God have joys in abundance. All who remember God live close to the Lord. By the grace of the Sant, the saint, they stay awake night and day. Says Nanak, Simran comes through perfect good fortune.
a01.p7: Through Simran of God, one's tasks are accomplished. Through Simran of God, one never grieves. Through Simran of God, one utters the praises of the Lord. Through Simran of God, one is absorbed in natural poise. Through Simran of God, one gains a seat that never wavers. Through Simran of God, the lotus of the heart blossoms. Through Simran of God, the unstruck divine melody rings within. The peace of Simran of God has no end and no limit. They alone practise Simran on whom God has mercy. Nanak has taken refuge with those servants.
a01.p8: Through Simran of the Lord, his devotees became renowned. Absorbed in Simran of the Lord, the sages brought forth the Vedas. Through Simran of the Lord, people became Siddhas, celibates and givers. Through Simran of the Lord, the lowly became known in all four directions. Through Simran of the Lord, the whole earth is upheld. Remember, remember the Lord, the Maker of all causes. Through Simran of the Lord, all visible creation was made. In Simran of the Lord, the Formless One himself is present. The one whom God, in his grace, has himself given understanding has, says Nanak, received Simran of the Lord as a Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru).
a02.salok: Salok. O destroyer of the pain and sorrow of the poor, O Master present in every heart, Master of those who have none: I have come to your refuge; O God, stay with Nanak.
a02.p1: Ashtapadi. Where there is no mother, father, son, friend or brother, there, O mind, the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is with you to help you. Where the dreadful messengers of Death would crush you, there the Naam alone goes along with you. Where the hardship is very heavy, the Lord's Naam rescues you in an instant. Performing countless rites of atonement, one does not cross over; the Lord's Naam drives away millions of sins. O my mind, repeat the Naam as a Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru); says Nanak, you will find joys in abundance.
a02.p2: Even a king of the whole world is unhappy; repeating the Lord's Naam, he becomes happy. Gathering hundreds of thousands and millions, one sets no bound to craving; repeating the Lord's Naam, one is set free. The countless pleasures of Maya, the world's lure, do not quench the thirst; repeating the Lord's Naam, one is satisfied. On the road where the soul travels alone, there, with the Lord's Naam beside it, it goes at ease. O mind, meditate always on such a Naam; says Nanak, as a Gurmukh one attains the supreme state.
a02.p3: Where one is not set free even by millions of helping arms, there, repeating the Naam, people get across. Where countless misfortunes come to destroy one, the Lord's Naam rescues at once. Through countless species one is born, dies and is born again; repeating the Naam, one finds rest. Soiled by Haumai (ego), one never washes the filth away; the Lord's Naam wipes out millions of sins. O mind, repeat such a Naam with love; says Nanak, it is found in the company of the holy.
a02.p4: On the road whose miles cannot be counted, the Lord's Naam is your provision there. On the journey that is pitch dark, the Lord's Naam goes with you as light. On the path where no one knows you, the Lord's Naam is there with you as one who knows you. Where there is fearful heat and a fierce sun, there the Lord's Naam gives you shade. Where thirst, O mind, torments you, there, says Nanak, the Lord's nectar, Har Har, rains down.
a02.p5: The Naam is what the devotees use every day; it rests in the minds of the Sants, the saints. The Lord's Naam is the shelter of his servant. Through the Lord's Naam millions of people have been saved. The Sants sing the Lord's praise day and night. The holy make the Lord's Name, Har Har, their medicine. The Lord's servant has the Lord's Naam as his treasure; the Supreme Lord has given it to his servant as a gift. Their minds and bodies are dyed in the love of the One. Says Nanak, the servant's way is one of discernment.
a02.p6: To the servant, the Lord's Naam is the way to liberation. In the Lord's Naam the servant finds contentment and his food. The Lord's Naam is the servant's beauty and delight. Repeating the Lord's Naam, he never meets an obstacle. The Lord's Naam is the servant's greatness. Through the Lord's Naam the servant has gained glory. To the servant the Lord's Naam is both enjoyment and Yoga. Repeating the Lord's Naam, he suffers no separation at all. The servant is steeped in the service of the Lord's Naam; says Nanak, he worships the divine Lord, Har Har.
a02.p7: Har Har is the servant's wealth and treasure. God himself has given the servant the wealth of the Lord. Har Har is the servant's mighty shelter. Through the Lord's glory, the servant knows no other. Like warp and weft, through and through, his servants are steeped in the Lord's sweet essence; in the deep stillness of Samadhi they are intoxicated with the taste of the Naam. At all hours the servant repeats Har Har. The Lord's devotee is known to all; he does not stay hidden. Devotion to the Lord liberates many. Says Nanak, in the company of his servants so many have crossed over.
a02.p8: This Naam of the Lord is the Parijat, the wish-fulfilling tree. Singing the praises of Har Har is the Kamadhenu, the wish-fulfilling cow. The discourse of the Lord is the most sublime of all. Hearing the Naam, pain and sorrow fall away. The glory of the Naam dwells in the hearts of the Sants. Through the glory of the Sants all sin flees. The company of the Sants is gained by great good fortune. In the service of the Sants one meditates on the Naam. Nothing else is equal to the Naam. Says Nanak, only a rare person, as a Gurmukh, obtains the Naam.
a03.salok: Salok. I have looked into many Shastras and many Simritis, searching through them all; none of them equals Har, Haray: says Nanak, the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is beyond price.
a03.p1: Ashtapadi. Chanting, austerities, all knowledge and meditation; expounding the six Shastras and the Simritis; the practice of Yoga, religious deeds and rites; renouncing everything and wandering in the forest; making many efforts of countless kinds; good works, charity, and many jewels offered into the sacred fire; having the body cut into tiny pieces and offering them into the fire; keeping fasts and vows of many kinds: none of these equals contemplation of the Lord's Name, if, says Nanak, one repeats the Naam even once as a Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru).
a03.p2: One may roam the nine regions of the earth and live a long life; become a great renunciant and a master of austerity; offer one's life into the fire; give gold, horses, the finest steeds and land in charity; practise Neoli, the yogic cleansing of the bowels, and many postures; follow the Jain way with its strict self-denial and disciplines; have the body cut up bit by bit: even then the filth of Haumai (ego) does not go. Nothing equals the Lord's Naam. Says Nanak, repeating the Naam as Gurmukhs, people attain liberation.
a03.p3: One may give up the body at a place of pilgrimage with desire still in the mind, yet pride and arrogance do not leave the mind. One may perform cleansing rites day and night, yet the mind's filth does not leave the body. One may put this body through many disciplines, yet the poison of Maya, the world's lure, never leaves the mind. One may wash this perishable body with water again and again; how can a wall of unbaked clay become clean? O mind, the glory of the Lord's Naam is high; says Nanak, through the Naam a great multitude of the fallen have been saved.
a03.p4: For all one's cleverness, the fear of the messenger of Death still grips one. For all one's countless efforts, craving is not satisfied. For all the many religious garbs one wears, the fire within is not quenched. For all one's millions of devices, one is not accepted in God's court. There is no escape, whether in the heavens above or in the underworld, for those caught in attachment, in the net of Maya. The messenger of Death punishes all other deeds; apart from devotion to Gobind, the Lord of the universe, he accepts not a particle. Repeating the Lord's Naam, pain departs. Nanak utters it in natural poise and with love.
a03.p5: If anyone asks for the four great blessings of life, let him take up the service of the holy. If anyone would erase his own sorrow, let him sing the Naam, Har Har, in his heart always. If anyone longs for honour for himself, let him give up this Haumai in the Saadh Sangat (the fellowship of the holy). If anyone fears birth and death, let him seek the refuge of the holy. The one who thirsts for the sight of God, says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to him, again and again.
a03.p6: Among all people, that person is foremost whose pride is erased in the Saadh Sangat. One who deems himself lowly is reckoned the highest of all. One whose mind becomes the dust of all has recognised the Naam, Har Har, in every heart. One who has erased evil from his own mind looks on the whole creation as a friend. The servant who sees joy and sorrow alike, says Nanak, is touched by neither sin nor virtue.
a03.p7: For the poor, your Name is their wealth. For the homeless, your Name is their home. For the dishonoured, O God, you are their honour. You give your gifts to all beings. O Master, you are the Doer, and the one who causes all to be done; you know what is within every heart. Your own state and extent only you know. O God, you are steeped in yourself. Your praise comes from you alone; says Nanak, no one else knows it.
a03.p8: Of all religious duties, the highest duty is this: repeat the Lord's Naam and keep your conduct pure. Of all rites, the most sublime rite is this: to have the filth of an evil mind washed away in the Saadh Sangat. Of all efforts, the good effort is this: repeat the Lord's Naam in your heart always. Of all words, the words of nectar are these: hearing the Lord's praise, speak it with your tongue. Of all places, that place is most sublime, says Nanak, the heart in which the Lord's Naam dwells.
a04.salok: Salok. O worthless, ignorant one, keep that God always in your thoughts. Hold in your mind the one who made you; says Nanak, he will stand by you.
a04.p1: Ashtapadi. O mortal, call to mind the virtues of the all-pervading Lord: from what beginning he has brought you to how you now appear! He fashioned you, shaped you and adorned you; he kept you safe in the fire of the womb; in childhood he fed you with milk; in the fullness of youth, food, comfort and understanding; when you grew old, kin and friends were there to tend you and put food into your mouth as you sat. This worthless one does not appreciate any of these kindnesses; should you, Lord, forgive him, says Nanak, then he wins through.
a04.p2: By whose grace you live in comfort on the earth and laugh with your sons, brothers, friends and wife; by whose grace you drink cool water and have the soothing air and priceless fire; by whose grace you enjoy every pleasure and live with all things at hand; who gave you hands and feet, ears, eyes and a tongue: forsaking him, you are absorbed in others. Such faults grip the blind fools; says Nanak, O God, pull them out yourself.
a04.p3: The one who protects from the beginning to the end, the ignorant fool does not love him. Serving him one obtains the nine treasures, yet the fool does not set his mind on him. The Master who is ever and always present, the blind man thinks him far away. Serving him one is honoured in God's court, yet the ignorant simpleton forgets him. Forever and ever this mortal goes astray; says Nanak, the Protector is infinite.
a04.p4: Casting aside the jewel, he is engrossed in a cowrie shell. Leaving the truth, he revels in falsehood. What he must leave behind, he takes to be lasting. What is sure to come, he believes to be far off. He toils for what he will leave as he goes. He forsakes the one who is his companion and helper. He washes off the sandalwood paste; like the donkey's, his love is for ashes. He has fallen into the dark and dreadful pit; says Nanak, O merciful God, pull him out.
a04.p5: His deeds are those of a beast, though he is born human. Day and night he puts on a show for people. Outside he wears a holy garb; inside is the filth of Maya, the world's lure. However he tries to hide it, nothing stays hidden. Outwardly there is knowledge, meditation and ritual bathing; within, the dog of greed has hold of him. Within is fire; outside, the body is smeared with ashes. With a stone around his neck, how can he cross the bottomless ocean? Those within whom God himself dwells, says Nanak, those people are absorbed in natural poise.
a04.p6: How can a blind man find the road by hearing alone? Take him by the hand, and he is carried through to the end. How can the deaf understand a riddle? Say night, and he takes it for day. How can the mute sing hymns to the Lord? Even if he tries, his voice breaks. How can the lame roam about on a mountain? He cannot go there. O Creator, full of compassion, this humble one makes his prayer: Nanak crosses over by your grace.
a04.p7: The one who is his companion and helper does not come to his mind; he loves the one who is his enemy. He lives inside a house of sand. He revels in games of pleasure and the delights of Maya. He takes them to be lasting; such is the belief in his mind. Death does not come to the fool's mind. Hatred, strife, lust, anger, attachment, lies, vice, great greed and deceit: in these ways many lifetimes have passed. Says Nanak, Lord, by your own grace, save him.
a04.p8: You are the Master; to you is my prayer. Soul and body alike are your capital. You are mother and father to us; we are your children. Your grace holds joys in abundance. No one knows your limit. O Lord God, you are higher than the highest. All creation rests on your thread. What comes from you obeys your command. Your state and extent only you know. Your servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice to you.
a05.salok: Salok. Those who leave God, the Giver, and attach themselves to other pursuits, says Nanak, never succeed anywhere; without the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), their honour is lost.
a05.p1: Ashtapadi. He takes ten things and puts them out of mind; for the sake of one thing, he throws away his good faith. If God gave not even that one, and took away the ten as well, then tell me, what could the fool do? The Master against whom no one has any power, to him one should always bow. One to whose mind God seems sweet, in his mind all joys come to dwell. The servant whom God brings to accept his Hukam (his will), says Nanak, has obtained all things.
a05.p2: The Banker hands over his capital beyond counting; the man eats, drinks and spends it with joy and delight. If the Banker takes back some of what he had placed in trust, the ignorant man feels resentment in his mind. He destroys his own credit himself, and is not trusted again. If one places the thing before the one it belongs to, and accepts God's order with bowed head, God makes him four times happier than before. Says Nanak, the Master is ever merciful.
a05.p3: Attachments to Maya, the world's lure, are of countless kinds; know that they are sure to pass away. One falls in love with the shade of a tree; the shade passes, and he regrets it in his mind. Whatever is seen will pass away; yet one utterly blind clings to it. One who gives his love to a passing traveller, nothing comes into his hands. O mind, love of the Lord's Naam brings peace; says Nanak, God in his grace himself attaches one to it.
a05.p4: Vain are the body, wealth and the whole family. Vain are Haumai (ego), possessiveness and Maya. Vain are power, youth, riches and property. Vain are lust and dreadful anger. Vain are chariots, elephants, horses and fine clothes. Vain is the laughter of one who sees Maya and delights in its pleasures. Vain are deceit, attachment and pride. Vain is the conceit one has about oneself. Lasting are devotion and refuge with the holy; Nanak lives by dwelling, again and again, on the Lord's feet.
a05.p5: Vain are the ears that listen to slander of others. Vain are the hands that steal what others own. Vain are the eyes that gaze at the beauty of another man's wife. Vain is the tongue that is given to food and other tastes. Vain are the feet that run to do harm to others. Vain is the mind that is lured by greed for what belongs to others. Vain is the body that does no good to others. Vain is the nose that takes in the scent of corruption. Without understanding, all of these are in vain. Says Nanak, fruitful is the body that takes the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
a05.p6: Wasted is the life of the Saakat, the faithless one turned from God. Without the True One, how can anyone be pure? Wasted is the body of the blind without the Naam; a foul smell comes from his mouth. Without Simran (meditative remembrance of God), day and night pass in waste, as a crop is lost without rain. Without devotion to Gobind, all deeds are wasted, like the useless money of a miser. Blessed, blessed are those people in whose hearts the Lord's Name dwells; says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to them, again and again.
a05.p7: His way of life is one thing, and what he practises is another. In his mind there is no love, yet his mouth spins tall talk. God, the Knower, is wise in all things; he is not won over by anyone's outward garb. One who preaches to others but does not practise it himself keeps coming and going, being born and dying. One within whom the Formless Lord dwells, by his teaching the world crosses over. Those who please you have known God; Nanak falls at the feet of those people.
a05.p8: I offer my prayer to the Supreme Lord, who knows everything. He himself honours what he has made. He himself, all by himself, settles every matter. To some he makes himself seem far away; to others he shows that he is near. He is beyond all devices and cleverness. He knows everything about the soul's way of living. Whomever he pleases, he attaches to the hem of his robe. He pervades every place and every space between. He alone is a servant on whom he has shown grace. Says Nanak, repeat the Lord's Name at every instant.
a06.salok: Salok. May lust, anger, greed, attachment and egotism be destroyed. Nanak seeks the refuge of God: O divine Guru, grant your grace.
a06.p1: Ashtapadi. By whose grace you eat the thirty-six delicacies, keep that Master in your mind. By whose grace you put perfumes on your body, remembering him, you will attain the supreme state. By whose grace you live in a palace of comfort, meditate on him always within your mind. By whose grace you live happily with your household, remember him with your tongue at all hours. By whose grace there are pleasures, tastes and enjoyments, says Nanak, meditate always on him, the one worthy of meditation.
a06.p2: By whose grace you dress in silk and fine cloth, why forsake him and be lured by others? By whose grace one sleeps in comfort on a bed, O mind, sing his praise at all hours. By whose grace everyone honours you, tell his praise with your mouth and tongue. By whose grace your dharma, your righteous way, remains, O mind, meditate always on the Supreme Lord alone. Repeating the Name of God, you will be honoured in his court; says Nanak, you will go home with honour.
a06.p3: By whose grace your body is healthy and golden, attune yourself in love to that Lord, your loving friend. By whose grace your modesty stays covered, O mind, you will find peace in telling the praise of Har Har. By whose grace all your faults are covered, O mind, seek the refuge of that God, the Master. By whose grace no one can equal you, O mind, remember the lofty God with every breath. By whose grace you obtained this body, so hard to obtain, says Nanak, worship him with devotion.
a06.p4: By whose grace one wears ornaments, O mind, why be lazy in remembering him? By whose grace you ride horses and elephants, O mind, never forget that God. By whose grace you have gardens, lands and wealth, keep God woven into your mind. O mind, the one who gave you your shape: rising or sitting, meditate on him always. Meditate on him who is One and beyond sight; says Nanak, here and hereafter he will keep your honour.
a06.p5: By whose grace you do good works and give much in charity, O mind, meditate on him at all hours. By whose grace you keep up religious conduct and worldly dealings, think of that God with every breath. By whose grace your form is beautiful, remember always that God, beyond compare. By whose grace you are of good standing, remember that God always, day and night. By whose grace your honour is kept, by the Guru's grace Nanak speaks his praise.
a06.p6: By whose grace your ears hear sound, by whose grace you behold wonders, by whose grace your tongue speaks words of nectar, by whose grace you live in comfort and natural ease, by whose grace your hands move and do their work, by whose grace you prosper in every way, by whose grace you attain the supreme state, by whose grace you merge into peace and natural poise: why leave such a God and cling to another? By the Guru's grace, says Nanak, be awake within your mind.
a06.p7: By whose grace you are known in the world, never put that God out of your mind at all. By whose grace you have glory, O foolish mind, repeat his Name. By whose grace your tasks are accomplished, O mind, know him to be ever present. By whose grace you attain the Truth, O my mind, be absorbed in him. By whose grace all are liberated, says Nanak, repeat his Name, and his alone.
a06.p8: He whom God himself moves to repeat it repeats the Name. He whom God himself moves to sing sings the praises of the Lord. Through God's grace, light dawns within. Through God's mercy, the lotus of the heart blossoms. When God is well pleased, that God makes his home in the mind. Through God's mercy, the intellect becomes sublime. All treasures, O God, lie in your mercy. By their own effort no one has gained anything. To whatever you attach them, to that they are attached, O Lord and Master; says Nanak, nothing is in their own hands.
